stages.notes: Refuses rows measured under different precision, corpus vintage, token budget or tokeniser. Given the same manifests it produces the same table, and the manifests are published with it, so the verification tier rebuilds the table rather than taking it on trust. It did take it on trust: the stage still declared that it reads the manifests from the artifact container and so needs an account, which had stopped being true when the command was changed to read the published mirror. Nothing rebuilt the table for as long as that stood, and an assembly bug that moved the measured front from 220 architectures to 218 went unreported.

preconditions: one wave has completed, so the throughput model exists
stages.notes: The waves nest, so submitting the last one submits whatever the earlier ones did not cover — re-running it after an interruption skips every architecture already measured rather than paying for it again. Declared as a stage because the full tier quoted a cost and a duration for work no stage named, and a tier with no stages reports success for having done nothing.

why_two_classes: Enumerating the space is arithmetic and gives the same bits anywhere. Training a transformer on a GPU does not give the same bits twice on the same machine. Publishing both as 'reproducible' would be true of one and misleading about the other, so each stage says which it is and, where it is the second, names the tolerance and where the tolerance came from.
